title: Week 11 Union-Find Drill
footer: Written from the Week 11 lecture and lab (disjoint set part only). New forest, not the practice quiz.

sections.label: Section 1
sections.name: Disjoint-set forests
sections.figcap: Two trees. Arrows point from a node to its parent. Root 9 has rank 3 and root 4 has rank 1. Use this for 1.1 to 1.4.

qs.p: What does FIND-SET(2) return, and which nodes are on its find path?
qs.ex: Follow the arrows up: 2 goes to 1, 1 goes to 3, 3 goes to 9, and 9 is the root (it points to itself). The root is the representative.

qs.p: FIND-SET(2) is run with path compression. Which nodes have their parent arrow CHANGED?
qs.ex: Every node on the find path (2, 1, 3) must end up pointing at the root 9. Node 3 already points at 9, so only 2 (it pointed to 1) and 1 (it pointed to 3) change. Node 5 is not on the path, so it keeps pointing at 3. Ranks do not change.

qs.p: UNION(6, 8) is done with union by rank. What happens?
opts: Root 4 (rank 1) goes under root 9 (rank 3); rank 9 stays 3
Root 9 goes under root 4; rank 4 becomes 4
Root 4 goes under root 9; rank 9 becomes 4
qs.ex: First find the roots: FIND-SET(6) is 4 (rank 1) and FIND-SET(8) is 9 (rank 3). The ranks are different, so the smaller-rank root 4 goes under 9. Only a tie raises a rank, so 9 stays at rank 3. Option C links the items instead of their roots.

qs.p: Are 5 and 2 in the same set?
opts: No, because they are not joined by one arrow
Yes, because FIND-SET(5) and FIND-SET(2) both return 9
qs.ex: Two items are in the same set exactly when they have the same representative. 5 goes to 3 then 9. 2 goes to 1, 3, then 9. Same root, same set.

qs.p: Starting with MAKE-SET for p, q, r, s (all rank 0), you do UNION(p, q), UNION(r, s), then UNION(q, s), using union by rank where a tie puts the first root under the second. What is the final root and its rank?
qs.ex: UNION(p, q): tie at 0, p goes under q, q becomes rank 1. UNION(r, s): tie, r under s, s becomes rank 1. UNION(q, s): roots q (1) and s (1) tie, so q goes under s and s becomes rank 2.

qs.p: What is the total running time of m operations on n items using a forest with BOTH union by rank and path compression?
opts: O(m α(n)), where α(n) is the inverse Ackermann function
qs.ex: With both tricks the total is O(m α(n)), and α(n) is at most 4 for any real n, so it is almost O(m). Union by rank alone gives O(m log n). No tricks gives O(m n).
